rationale: Surfaced by the 024 US5 de-suppression, which narrowed `drop_absent_optional` to deacon's side. While the rule ran on BOTH sides, an authored null, an authored empty collection and an omitted property all normalized to 'the key is absent on both sides', so the three FR-055 states produced ONE observation and the difference could not be seen. SHRUNK BY #398, which wrapped every modeled optional — including the eleven properties previously typed as bare collections — in `Option` with `skip_serializing_if`. Re-measured at oracle 0.87.0 on `fx-us5-null-empty-omitted`: `configuration.forwardPorts`, `configuration.containerEnv` and `nullEmptyOmitted.mounts` now AGREE, so their tolerances were DELETED rather than narrowed — a tolerance whose difference stopped reproducing is stale by design, and leaving it would suppress the next real difference on that path. WHAT IS STILL TOLERATED is the authored `"name": null`, on the raw key and on the derived FR-055 classification: deacon holds an authored null and an omission in the same `None`, so omitting unauthored optionals necessarily omits authored nulls too. That boundary MOVED rather than closed — before the fix both CLIs emitted `null` here and AGREED — which the pre-#398 version of this waiver predicted in as many words. Net: deacon went from ~40 unconditionally emitted keys to the 2 the reference emits for a minimal configuration, and the residual is one schema-invalid input shape. This remains a fidelity DEFECT, not a design choice, tracked at #398 with the remaining scope named there. Scoped to the named paths on the one case authored to demonstrate them; self-invalidates the moment a difference stops reproducing.
